summary: Applies a one-frame Bullet force pulse that instantly changes affected body velocities, useful for kicks, impacts, launches, or other short-duration physics events.

key_params.name: pulse
key_params.note: Applies the impulse force on the next simulation frame

key_params.name: force
key_params.note: Linear force in Newtons applied by the pulse

key_params.name: relpos
key_params.note: Force application point relative to the physical center of the body

key_params.name: torque
key_params.note: Rotational force applied by the pulse

key_params.name: parentshortcut
key_params.note: Common COMP shortcut for accessing the component from children

key_params.name: opshortcut
key_params.note: Global OP shortcut for accessing the component anywhere

key_concepts: Impulse Force COMP applies a Bullet force pulse for one simulation frame when Pulse Force is triggered.
The pulse instantly changes affected body velocities and then stops affecting the simulation unless pulsed again.
An impulse with a given Newton value produces the same velocity change as an active Force COMP with the same value applied for exactly one second.
Force defines the linear impulse, Torque defines rotational impulse, and Relative Position can add rotation by applying force away from the physical center.
Impulse Force COMP is intended for discrete events such as kicks, launches, impacts, or cannon-like shots rather than continuous acceleration.
common_gotchas: Impulse Force COMP has no effect until its Pulse Force parameter is pulsed.
The force is applied for one frame and then stops; pulse again for repeated hits.
Resulting velocity is equivalent to applying the same active force for one second, but the change happens instantly.
A non-zero Relative Position can add rotation because the impulse is not applied at the physical center.
The impulse must be referenced by the relevant Bullet simulation setup to affect actors.
For continuous acceleration, use Force COMP rather than repeatedly pulsing Impulse Force COMP unless a discrete event is intended.
